extracted.intended_audience: Small business applicants preparing SBIR/STTR proposals for DOD, NASA (and general SBIR applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on agency-specific evaluation criteria used to review SBIR/STTR proposals (particularly DOD and NASA), plus cross-agency considerations and common application components and failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (Universal SBIR Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is a criterion present in all SBIR/STTR solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators across agencies expect the proposed work to demonstrate novelty and meaningful advancement over existing approaches; innovation is a core, cross-cutting evaluation factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience, Qualifications and Facilities (Universal SBIR Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience, Qualifications and Facilities is another common evaluation criterion across all SBIR/STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes PI and key personnel qualifications, institutional facilities and resources, and the team's ability to execute the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness, Technical Merit and Innovation of the Proposed Approach (DOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of the proposed innovation; Originality and significance of approach; Likelihood of overcoming technical challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD reviewers evaluate whether the technical approach is sound, technically meritorious, original and significant, and whether proposed methods are likely to surmount anticipated technical risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the Proposed Principal/Key Investigators, Supporting Staff and Consultants (DOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record; Relevant expertise; Team composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD examines the PI/Key Investigators' and team's demonstrated experience and expertise relevant to the project and whether the team composition is adequate to accomplish objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for Commercial Applications (DOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government or private sector applications; Benefits expected from commercialization; Path to deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD looks for plausible commercial or government uses, realistic benefits from commercialization, and a credible path to transition/deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific/Technical Merit and Feasibility (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of what is proposed; Soundness of approach; Achievability of objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA reviewers judge the scientific/technical merit and whether the proposed objectives are feasible within the project scope and timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience, Qualifications and Facilities (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical capabilities and experience of PI, project manager, key personnel, staff, consultants and subcontractors; Consistency with the research effort; Degree of commitment and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA emphasizes personnel capability, alignment of team expertise with tasks, and demonstrated commitment/availability to carry out the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of the Proposed Work Plan (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan structure and timeline; Milestones and deliverables; Risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess whether the work plan is well-structured with realistic timelines, clear milestones/deliverables, and adequate identification and mitigation of risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Potential and Feasibility (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offeror's experience and record in technology commercialization; Co-funding commitments from private or non-SBIR/non-STTR funding sources; Existing and projected commitments for Phase III funding; Initial commercialization strategy for the innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA gives weight to demonstrated commercialization experience, outside co-funding, credible Phase III funding commitments, and a concrete initial commercialization strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price Reasonableness (NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic budget; Cost-benefit; Allocation across categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA evaluates whether the proposed budget is realistic and cost-effective, and whether costs are reasonably allocated across budget categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept feasibility; Smaller awards (~$50K-$300K); 6-12 month period; Concept proof, not full development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I proposals should focus on demonstrating feasibility of the concept within a short timeline and modest budget; reviewers expect proof-of-concept results rather than full development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Build on Phase I results; Larger awards (~$750K-$2M); 24-month period typical; Significant prototyping/development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase II reviewers expect substantive development and prototyping that advance the Phase I results toward commercialization and technical maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization; Government or private sector; Sole-source contracts allowed; No additional SBIR funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase III is focused on transitioning the innovation to commercial or government use, often via non-SBIR funding or sole-source contracts; proposals should demonstrate commercialization pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH SBIR Specific Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Health-related innovations; Similar review process to R-series with commercialization addendum; Commercialization plan weighted equally to research plan; NIH study sections plus commercial/regulatory experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NIH SBIR, expect scientific peer review akin to R-series grants augmented by commercialization review; the commercialization plan carries equal weight with the scientific plan and reviewers include regulatory/commercial experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF SBIR Specific Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer discovery (I-Corps style) heavily weighted; Innovation considered broadly (including business model); Less prescriptive on technical methodology; Often stronger commercialization emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF places heavy emphasis on evidence of customer discovery and market understanding, accepts broader definitions of innovation (e.g., business model), and prioritizes commercialization readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Reasons for SBIR Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak commercialization plan; Unclear technical innovation; Missing or weak Customer Discovery evidence; Wrong topic for solicitation; Budget mismatch with scope; Unqualified team; Failure to address agency-specific priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these common pitfalls by presenting a clear commercialization pathway, unambiguous technical innovation, documented customer discovery, aligned budget/scope, qualified personnel, and explicit alignment with the solicitation's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Components (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover sheet; Project Summary; Technical Proposal (~25 pages); Cost/Budget; Commercialization Plan (Phase II especially); Letters of support (customers, partners); Bios/CVs; Subcontractor information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all listed components are complete and tailored to agency expectations (e.g., a strong commercialization plan for Phase II, concise technical proposal of the expected length, and letters demonstrating partnerships or customer interest).
